_about:
WHAT AUTO-TAGGING LOOKS FOR in a scene's action lines (PRD 2.0 FR-603). Read by src/lib/screenplay-analysis.js `suggestElements()`. Content, not code, for invariant 2.

CAST is not in this file: a character is whoever has a CUE in the scene, plus anybody introduced in capitals in the action ("RAVI, 30s, counts coins") — the screenplay convention that a speaking part is capitalised on first appearance. That needs no word list.

SOUND also reads the convention: a sound effect written in capitals in action ("the phone RINGS", "a GUNSHOT") is a cue, which is how a sound department breaks a script down. The words below catch the ones written in lower case.

Every entry is a lower-case whole word or phrase. Matching is whole-word, so `car` does not fire on `scarf` and `bus` does not fire on `business`. Tamil-production vocabulary (auto, lorry, two-wheeler, nadaswaram) is listed alongside English because that is how Chennai scripts are written.

A SUGGESTION IS NOT A TAG. The breakdown shows every suggestion with the line it came from and adds only what somebody accepts; nothing here writes to a scene by itself.

soundCaps._about: Words that, written IN CAPITALS in an action line, mark a sound cue by convention. Lower-case occurrences of the same words are ordinary prose and are not cues.
